title: Faithful semilinear action and stable Cartier pullback on an invariant open
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $L/e$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $H$ be a subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}_e(L)$, and let $B$ be an $e$-scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Put $Y=B\times_e\operatorname{Spec}L$ with projections $p:Y\to B$ and $s:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $X\subseteq Y$ be a nonempty open subscheme stable under every map $\alpha_h=\operatorname{id}_B\times\operatorname{Spec}(h^{-1})$ for $h\in H$, and put $u=p|_X$, $s_X=s|_X$. Suppose $u$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The restrictions $r_h=\alpha_h|_X$ define a left action of $H$ by $e$-scheme automorphisms of $X$, and $u\circ r_h=u$ and $s_X\circ r_h=\operatorname{Spec}(h^{-1})\circ s_X$ for all $h$. This action on the scheme $X$ is faithful, meaning that $r_h=\operatorname{id}_X$ implies $h=1$; the given action on $L$ is also faithful. For every effective Cartier divisor $D\subseteq B$ with ideal $\mathcal I_D$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], its pullback $D_X=D\times_B X$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X$, with support $u^{-1}|D|$ and ideal $\mathcal J=u^{-1}\mathcal I_D\cdot\mathcal O_X$. It is stable as a divisor: $r_h^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal O_X=\mathcal J$ for every $h\in H$. The empty effective Cartier divisor is allowed. No finiteness, separability, normality, properness or integrality assumption is imposed on $L/e$ or $X$.

proof.text: Write $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$. By contravariant functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ and the fibre-product universal property, $\alpha_1=1$, $\alpha_h\circ\alpha_k=\alpha_{hk}$, $p\circ\alpha_h=p$ and $s\circ\alpha_h=\operatorname{Spec}(h^{-1})\circ s$. For the second projection of the composite, $s\circ\alpha_h\circ\alpha_k=\operatorname{Spec}(h^{-1})\circ\operatorname{Spec}(k^{-1})\circ s=\operatorname{Spec}(k^{-1}\circ h^{-1})\circ s=\operatorname{Spec}((hk)^{-1})\circ s$; its first projection is $p$. Uniqueness in the fibre-product property gives the action law. Since $h$ fixes $e$, these are $e$-morphisms. Stability for both $h$ and $h^{-1}$ gives $\alpha_h(X)=X$. Restrict the continuous map and its structure-sheaf maps to this open: $\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_Y|_X$, so this defines $r_h$ and $j\circ r_h=\alpha_h\circ j$. The same restriction for $h^{-1}$ is its inverse. Restricting the identities above gives $r_1=1$, $r_h\circ r_k=r_{hk}$ and the two required formulas for $u$ and $s_X$.

proof.text: If $r_h=1$, the preceding formula gives $s_X=\operatorname{Spec}(h^{-1})\circ s_X$. Choose $x\in X$, using nonemptiness. The structure map induces $\lambda:L\to\kappa(x)$; the residue field of the sole point of $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is $L$. By clause (2) of the spectrum-map naturality lemma with $R=R'=L$, $\psi=h^{-1}$ and the zero prime, $\operatorname{Spec}(h^{-1})$ induces $h^{-1}$ on this residue field $L$. Applying the maps on stalks and then their residue quotients to this equality gives $\lambda=\lambda\circ h^{-1}$, since the stalk map of a composite is the composite of the stalk maps. Explicitly, a scalar $a\in L$ has residue $\lambda(a)$ under $s_X$, whereas the composite sends it to $\lambda(h^{-1}(a))$. The field homomorphism $\lambda$ is injective: if $a\ne0$ were in its kernel, $1=\lambda(aa^{-1})=0$. Thus $h^{-1}(a)=a$ for every $a\in L$, so $h=1$. The evaluation action on $L$ itself is faithful because $H$ is a subgroup of its automorphism group: an element fixing every scalar is the identity automorphism.

proof.text: Apply the flat Cartier-pullback theorem to $g=u:X\to B$ and $D\subseteq B$: its only additional hypothesis is precisely the assumed flatness of $u$. It gives that $D_X=D\times_BX$ is effective Cartier. Its local formula says that on affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq u^{-1}(W)$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq B$, with $\mathcal I_D|_W=(t)$, the ideal of $D_X$ is $(\varphi(t))\subseteq A$, where $\varphi:R\to A$ is induced by $u$. These formulas identify its ideal sheaf with $\mathcal J=u^{-1}\mathcal I_D\cdot\mathcal O_X$.

source.place: Tag 02OO, lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-defined, case (6) and the affine-local proof; Tag 01WV, definition-pullback-effective-Cartier-divisor.

proof.text: By the cited description of the map of spectra on points, on the same affine charts, a point with prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset A$ lies in $|D_X|$ exactly when $\varphi(t)\in\mathfrak q$, equivalently $t\in\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, exactly when its image in $B$ lies in $|D|$. Thus $|D_X|=u^{-1}|D|$. For invariance, $u\circ r_h=u$ makes each $u^{-1}W$ stable. On it $\mathcal J$ is generated by $u^\sharp(t)$. The extended inverse-image ideal along $r_h$ is generated there by $r_h^\sharp(u^\sharp(t))=(u\circ r_h)^\sharp(t)=u^\sharp(t)$. Hence $r_h^{-1}\mathcal J\cdot\mathcal O_X=\mathcal J$ on this open cover and therefore globally. This is equality of ideal sheaves, so preserves the divisor with its scheme structure. The unit generator $t=1$ covers the empty divisor case, giving $\mathcal J=\mathcal O_X$ and empty support.
